title: Add existing VPC partial adoption mode (consume subnet IDs) + guardrails; update docs
author: Bruno Silva
description:
Context: Several pilot/prospect environments cannot create a new VPC and must deploy Redwood Private into an existing shared VPC (often with TGW, centralized egress, and strict controls). This PR adds a supported 'partial adoption' mode where `modules/redwood-private-vpc` (and underlying modules where applicable) can consume existing VPC + subnet IDs instead of creating VPC/subnets/route tables. This is intentionally scoped to networking primitives only; we still manage endpoints, SGs, and flow logs according to module inputs.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced an explicit adoption switch for the wrapper module: `create_vpc` (default true). When false, the module requires `existing_vpc_id` and one or more subnet ID lists (private and/or isolated; public optional).
- Added input contract + validation/guardrails to prevent unsafe or ambiguous combinations, including:
  - Disallow enabling NAT creation (`nat_mode` != "none") when `create_vpc=false` (we do not create/own NAT gateways/EIPs in an existing VPC).
  - Disallow `enable_public_subnets=true` when `create_vpc=false` (public subnet creation/IGW/RT changes are out of scope).
  - Enforce that `existing_private_subnet_ids` and `existing_isolated_subnet_ids` (when both set) are disjoint.
  - Require at least 2 subnets for interface endpoints when `enable_vpc_endpoints=true` and `private_dns_enabled=true` (to avoid single-AZ fragility) with a clear error.
  - Require that all supplied subnet IDs are in the same VPC (validated via data lookups) and that the VPC region matches provider region.
- Adjusted outputs contract to stay stable for the installer: `vpc_id`, `private_subnet_ids`, `isolated_subnet_ids`, `endpoint_ids`, `security_group_ids` always resolve, regardless of create vs adopt.
- Updated docs and examples:
  - Added "Existing VPC adoption" section to `modules/redwood-private-vpc/README.md` with a minimal tfvars example and a list of explicit non-goals.
  - Added troubleshooting notes for common misconfigs (missing DNS support in VPC; subnets without required route to S3 gateway endpoint; locked-down NACLs blocking endpoint ENIs).
  - Updated module matrix notes to call out that VPC/subnet creation is optional but endpoints/SG/flow logs remain managed.

Non-goals / intentionally unsupported in this PR:
- Creating/modifying route tables, IGW attachments, NAT gateways, or NACLs in an existing VPC.
- Automatically discovering "the right" subnets from tags; subnet IDs must be provided explicitly.
- Multi-VPC / shared services VPC bridging patterns beyond consuming IDs.

Testing:
- Extended integration harness to cover `create_vpc=false` (plan-only in CI using stubbed data for subnet/VPC lookups; apply test remains create_vpc=true to keep ephemeral costs predictable).
- Added unit-style validation tests via `terraform validate` on example configurations.

Notes for installer integration:
- Installer can keep consuming the same outputs. When using adoption mode, ensure preflight checks are run for endpoint reachability + VPC DNS support (this PR links docs to the runbook).

Docs reviewers: Please focus on the "guardrails" section and confirm we are explicit about what we do NOT manage in existing VPC mode.

Security reviewers: Please confirm the disallowed combinations cover the foot-guns we observed in SUP-2197 (image pull failures due to missing endpoints and assumptions around egress).
commits: modules/redwood-private-vpc: add create_vpc flag + existing_* inputs
modules/redwood-private-vpc: add validations and explicit error messages for unsafe combos
modules/vpc-endpoints: allow passing subnet_ids explicitly (no dependency on vpc-baseline outputs)
examples/aws/private-vpc: add existing-vpc-adoption example tfvars + README
ci: add plan matrix job for create_vpc=false adoption mode
ci_summary: Checks: terraform fmt (pass), terraform validate (pass), tflint (pass), checkov (pass with 1 documented skip for VPC endpoint policy stub), integration test (apply create_vpc=true: pass), integration test (plan create_vpc=false: pass). One transient failure on first run due to AWS API throttling in integration apply job; rerun succeeded.
review_conversation:
Victor Alvarez (review): In existing VPC mode, we should be very strict about not trying to infer route tables / public/private semantics. Please make sure we never create IGW/NAT/RT changes when create_vpc=false. Also, can we validate that subnets are all in the same VPC?

Bruno Silva (author): Agree. I removed any conditional paths that could create IGW/NAT/RT resources when create_vpc=false and added explicit validation: we data lookup each subnet -> vpc_id and assert they match `existing_vpc_id`. Also added an error if `nat_mode` is set when create_vpc=false.

Irene Choi (review): The guardrail list is good, but please add an explicit disallow for enable_public_subnets in adoption mode. Also, for endpoints, we should require at least 2 subnets if private DNS is enabled; otherwise we have single-AZ fragility and weird DNS behavior during maintenance.

Bruno Silva (author): Added both. `enable_public_subnets` now errors when create_vpc=false. Added a precondition for endpoints + private_dns requiring >= 2 subnet IDs. Docs updated to explain why.

Marcus Lin (review): Security perspective: do we risk users enabling endpoints without attaching endpoint policies and assuming they're locked down? I see "policy stubs" but want docs to say default policies are permissive and customers should restrict. Also, call out that NACLs are not managed.

Bruno Silva (author): Updated README: endpoint policies default to AWS default (no explicit restriction). Added a section "Hardening" with a snippet showing how to pass endpoint policies, and a clear note that we do not manage NACLs and that customers must ensure NACLs allow endpoint ENI traffic.

Ethan Park (review): Installer expects `private_subnet_ids` to always be populated. What happens if a customer only supplies isolated subnet IDs?

Bruno Silva (author): Good catch. Updated contract: at least one of private or isolated must be provided, but outputs always include both lists (empty list allowed). I added a validation that installer-required components should use private subnets; docs now say isolated-only is not supported for current alpha unless you run a custom control-plane config.

Kira Thompson (review): Docs: please add a short table of "Supported in existing VPC mode" vs "Not supported" and a troubleshooting note for VPC DNS attributes (enableDnsSupport/enableDnsHostnames) since that bites folks on private endpoints.

Bruno Silva (author): Added the table and the DNS troubleshooting note + link to the networking preflight runbook.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI: The new plan-only job is great. Please ensure it doesn't require AWS credentials with broad permissions (we should be able to run terraform validate/plan with minimal). Also, checkov skip needs a justification.

Bruno Silva (author): Adjusted workflow so adoption-mode plan uses a local test fixture and does not hit AWS. Added checkov skip comment with rationale (endpoint policy is intentionally left as customer-provided input; default is AWS-managed behavior).

Victor Alvarez (final): LGTM after the latest guardrails. Please keep the error messages actionable.

Marcus Lin (final): Approved with doc updates. Make sure we include this as a supported topology in the alpha overview docs.

Merge: Squash merged by Irene Choi.
release_notes: Terraform modules (alpha): Added supported 'existing VPC' adoption mode to `redwood-private-vpc` wrapper to consume pre-created VPC and subnet IDs. Added strict validation to prevent unsafe combinations (no NAT/public subnet creation in adoption mode) and expanded docs/examples for locked-down enterprise environments.
